nodes.summary: For a binary CSP $P$ with finitely many variables and domains $\mathrm{dom}$, AC-3 on the whole problem is AC-3 run from $\mathrm{dom}$ with the queue initialized to the arc list of $P$; it returns the final domains together with the number of revisions performed.
nodes.title: AC-3 on the whole problem

nodes.summary: For a binary CSP $P$ with finitely many variables, domains $\mathrm{dom}$, a queue $q$ of pairs of variables and a variable $v$, the domain of $v$ returned by AC-3 run from $\mathrm{dom}$ with queue $q$ is a subset of $\mathrm{dom}(v)$.
nodes.title: AC-3 only shrinks domains

nodes.summary: For a binary CSP $P$ with finitely many variables, domains $\mathrm{dom}$ and a queue $q$ of pairs of variables, the number of revisions AC-3 performs from $\mathrm{dom}$ with queue $q$ is at most the potential $\ell + \sum_x |\mathrm{dom}(x)| \cdot \mathrm{indeg}(x)$, where $\ell$ is the length of $q$ and $\mathrm{indeg}(x)$ is the number of entries of the arc list of $P$ ending at $x$.
nodes.title: AC-3 revisions are bounded by the potential

nodes.summary: For a binary CSP $P$ with finitely many variables and initial domains $\mathrm{dom}$, AC-3 run from $\mathrm{dom}$ with every arc of $P$ queued performs at most $m + \sum_x |\mathrm{dom}(x)| \cdot \mathrm{indeg}(x)$ revisions, where $m$ is the length of the arc list of $P$ and $\mathrm{indeg}(x)$ is the number of entries of that list ending at $x$.
nodes.title: Bound on the number of AC-3 revisions

nodes.summary: Given a binary CSP $P$ with finitely many variables, domains $\mathrm{dom}$ and a queue $q$ of pairs of variables, AC-3 returns $\mathrm{dom}$ when $q$ is empty. Otherwise it removes the first pair $(x, y)$ of $q$ and revises it: the revised domain of $x$ consists of the values $a \in \mathrm{dom}(x)$ for which some $b \in \mathrm{dom}(y)$ has the arc $(x, y)$ allowing $x = a$ together with $y = b$. If the revised…
nodes.title: The AC-3 algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary CSP with finitely many variables whose constraints are symmetric, that is the arc $(x, y)$ allows $(a, b)$ exactly when the arc $(y, x)$ allows $(b, a)$, and whose arcs all join two distinct variables. Let $\mathrm{dom}$ be domains and $q$ a queue whose entries are arcs of $P$, such that every arc of $P$ not in $q$ is consistent with respect to $\mathrm{dom}$. Then every arc of $P$ is consistent…
nodes.title: Arc consistency invariant of AC-3

nodes.summary: AC-3 makes every arc consistent, for constraints given symmetrically on both orientations of an arc and arcs between distinct variables.
nodes.title: AC-3 makes every arc consistent

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary CSP whose constraints are symmetric, that is the arc $(x, y)$ allows $(a, b)$ exactly when the arc $(y, x)$ allows $(b, a)$. Let $\mathrm{dom}$ be domains, let $x \ne y$ be variables, let $R$ be the set of values $a \in \mathrm{dom}(x)$ for which some $b \in \mathrm{dom}(y)$ has the arc $(x, y)$ allowing $x = a$ together with $y = b$, and let $\mathrm{dom}'$ be $\mathrm{dom}$ with the domain of…
nodes.title: Arc consistency after one AC-3 revision

nodes.summary: Given a binary CSP $P$ and domains $\mathrm{dom}$, an arc $(x, y)$ is consistent when for every value $a \in \mathrm{dom}(x)$ there is a value $b \in \mathrm{dom}(y)$ such that the arc $(x, y)$ allows $x = a$ together with $y = b$.
nodes.title: Arc consistency

nodes.summary: A binary constraint satisfaction problem with variables in $X$ and values in $D$ consists of a finite list of directed arcs $(x, y)$ with $x, y \in X$, and, for all variables $x, y$ and values $a, b \in D$, a Boolean saying whether the arc $(x, y)$ allows $x = a$ together with $y = b$.
nodes.title: Binary constraint satisfaction problem

nodes.summary: For a binary constraint satisfaction problem $P$ and a variable $x$, the in-degree of $x$ is the number of arcs $(z, x)$ of $P$ ending at $x$, counted with multiplicity in the list of arcs of $P$.
nodes.title: In-degree of a variable

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary constraint satisfaction problem with finitely many variables, $\mathrm{dom}$ finite domains for its variables, and $q$ a queue of arcs each of which is an arc of $P$. Then every solution $\sigma$ of $P$ within $\mathrm{dom}$ is also a solution of $P$ within the domains returned by AC-3 started from $\mathrm{dom}$ with queue $q$.
nodes.title: No solution is lost

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary constraint satisfaction problem with variables $X$ and values $D$, and give each variable $x$ a finite domain $\mathrm{dom}(x) \subseteq D$. An assignment $\sigma : X \to D$ is a solution of $P$ within $\mathrm{dom}$ when $\sigma(x) \in \mathrm{dom}(x)$ for every variable $x$ and, for every arc $(x, y)$ of $P$, the arc $(x, y)$ allows the pair $(\sigma(x), \sigma(y))$.
nodes.title: Solution of a binary CSP within given domains

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary constraint satisfaction problem with finitely many variables and $\mathrm{dom}$ finite domains for its variables. If $\sigma$ is a solution of $P$ within $\mathrm{dom}$, then for every variable $v$ the value $\sigma(v)$ lies in the domain of $v$ returned by AC-3 run from $\mathrm{dom}$ with all arcs of $P$ queued.
nodes.title: Solutions survive AC-3

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary constraint satisfaction problem, $\mathrm{dom}$ finite domains for its variables and $\sigma$ a solution of $P$ within $\mathrm{dom}$. For every arc $(x, y)$ of $P$, the value $\sigma(x)$ lies in the revision of the arc $(x, y)$ with respect to $\mathrm{dom}$.
nodes.title: Revision keeps solution values

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary constraint satisfaction problem with finitely many variables and $\mathrm{dom}$ finite domains for its variables. If AC-3, run from $\mathrm{dom}$ with all arcs of $P$ queued, returns the empty domain for some variable $v$, then no assignment $\sigma$ is a solution of $P$ within $\mathrm{dom}$.
nodes.title: An emptied domain rules out solutions

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary constraint satisfaction problem with finitely many variables, $\mathrm{dom}$ finite domains for its variables, $x$ and $y$ variables and $q$ a queue of arcs. Suppose the revision $R$ of the arc $(x, y)$ with respect to $\mathrm{dom}$ differs from $\mathrm{dom}(x)$, and let $\mathrm{dom}'$ agree with $\mathrm{dom}$ except that $\mathrm{dom}'(x) = R$. Then the potential of $\mathrm{dom}'$ with the…
nodes.title: A shrinking revision lowers the potential

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary constraint satisfaction problem with finitely many variables, $\mathrm{dom}$ finite domains for its variables and $q$ a queue of arcs. The potential of $\mathrm{dom}$ and $q$ is
nodes.title: Termination potential of AC-3

nodes.summary: For a binary constraint satisfaction problem $P$ and variables $x$ and $y$, the arcs requeued after revising $(x, y)$ are the arcs $(z, x)$ of $P$ with $z \neq y$, in their order in the list of arcs of $P$.
nodes.title: Arcs requeued after a revision

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a binary constraint satisfaction problem with values $D$, $\mathrm{dom}$ finite domains for its variables, and $x$, $y$ variables. The revision of the arc $(x, y)$ is the set of values $a \in \mathrm{dom}(x)$ that have a support in the domain of $y$: some $b \in \mathrm{dom}(y)$ such that the arc $(x, y)$ allows the pair $(a, b)$.
nodes.title: Revision of an arc

nodes.summary: A binary constraint satisfaction problem is symmetric when, for all variables $x, y$ and values $a, b$, the constraint on the ordered pair $(x, y)$ allows $x = a$ together with $y = b$ exactly when the constraint on $(y, x)$ allows $y = b$ together with $x = a$.
nodes.title: Symmetric binary CSP

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
